about: A check of every factual claim in the two study-section drafts of MV's follow-up and README's first screen (mv/landing-kit/section-mv-followup.txt, section-readme-first-screen.txt) against the branch mv-land at 416b0af81, by one checker per draft; each finding then given to a skeptic told to refute it. A finding the skeptic confirms (real) was taken into the drafts, BOUNDARY-FIELD, the screen or the tests; a refuted one was left, with the skeptic's reason.

findings.claim: Evidence: "after the fixes, the dumps of core receipts 20261030T232750.486801Z, 20261031T013649.265381Z and 20261031T054654.692180Z and of U4's build give the same auxiliaries, walks, forwarders, laws and root constants under the rule before and after them, and outside is empty (... reports/boundary-rule-compare.json, by boundary/check/compare_rule.py)"
findings.problem: The cited report and script cover two of the four dumps. Nothing on the branch backs 232750 or U4's build.
findings.evidence: reports/boundary-rule-compare.json has exactly two runs: core_receipt 20261031T013649.265381Z and 20261031T054654.692180Z. compare_rule.py reads only the latest core receipt's dump (ml.load_measure(), ml.CORE), so it cannot run on U4's build. The only statement about 232750 and U4's build is BOUNDARY-FIELD §9's fourth-re-check paragraph; no output is kept (the scratch has only fwcmp4/boundary_prev.py, no result).
findings.fix: "after the fixes, the dumps of core receipts 20261031T013649.265381Z (RF-M.3's) and 20261031T054654.692180Z (HE2's) give the same ... and outside is empty ([reports/boundary-rule-compare.json], by boundary/check/compare_rule.py); at the fixes the same comparison on core 20261030T232750.486801Z and on U4's build gave the same, with no output kept." Alternatively, keep those two runs in the report.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. reports/boundary-rule-compare.json has exactly two runs, both old=26977f25a: core_receipt 20261031T013649.265381Z (52,346 constants) and 20261031T054654.692180Z (52,419). The section's figures match those two. compare_rule.py reads ml.load_measure() and ml.CORE, the checkout's latest core receipt, so it cannot cover U4's build as written. The only claim about 232750 and U4's build is in BOUNDARY-FIELD §9's fourth re-check paragraph, and no output for it exists on the branch. The scratch fwcmp4/ holds only boundary_prev.py, which is 26977f25a's boundary.py (sha e352cc16...), and no result.

findings.claim: "A fourth re-check ... found the eight taken and four more, all confirmed, none a regression and none on the current dump"
findings.problem: The report calls only R4-1 and R4-2 not regressions. R4-4 is §3.6 text that 26977f25a's own reorder left stale. R4-3 is a gap in the negatives that 26977f25a's §8 text claims.
findings.evidence: recheck4.json R4-1: "It is not a regression (1aa84fd59 gives the same)". R4-2: "It is not a regression (1aa84fd59 and 652ee90ac give the same)". R4-4: "§3.6 still describes the old order ... Since the reorder" and "The commit's diff of BOUNDARY-FIELD.md leaves §3.6 untouched". The lens (p10): "The only change: when every derived entry fails D1 to D5, the Lean check now runs (see R4-4)". R4-3 concerns §8's sentence written in 26977f25a.
findings.fix: "... four more, all confirmed: R4-1 and R4-2 are not regressions (1aa84fd59 gives the same) and are latent; R4-3 is a gap in the follow-up's own negatives, and R4-4 is §3.6 text its reorder left behind; none occurs on the current dump."

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In recheck4.json only R4-1 ("It is not a regression (1aa84fd59 gives the same False)") and R4-2 ("1aa84fd59 and 652ee90ac give the same") are called not regressions. R4-3 concerns §8's sentence about negatives, which first appears at 26977f25a; at 1aa84fd59 there is no "must not attach" text. R4-4 is §3.6 text that 26977f25a's reorder left stale ("Since the reorder", "The commit's diff of BOUNDARY-FIELD.md leaves §3.6 untouched"), and the lens lists it under "What the fixes break" (p10). No behaviour regressed, but the report does not support "none a regression" for R4-3 and R4-4. BOUNDARY-FIELD §9 makes the same claim ("None of the four is a regression").

findings.claim: Evidence: "the fourth re-check reproduced each of its findings on Lean 4.29.1"
findings.problem: R4-4 was not reproduced on Lean. Its verifier ran report() of both commits with a recording stub in place of the Lean check.
findings.evidence: recheck4.json R4-4 verdict: "It runs report() of 1aa84fd59 and of 26977f25a on the test's CONSTANTS, with a recording Lean stub, once running and once not running." The report's own `about` says only "which reproduced each", not on Lean 4.29.1. BOUNDARY-FIELD §9 repeats the overstatement.
findings.fix: "the fourth re-check's verifier reproduced each of its findings: R4-1 to R4-3 on Lean 4.29.1, R4-4 on report() with a stubbed check". Change §9 the same way.

verdict.reason: Confirmed for R4-4. Its verdict says the verifier "runs report() of 1aa84fd59 and of 26977f25a on the test's CONSTANTS, with a recording Lean stub" (the lens's p10 also shows toolchain 'T'), so it was not reproduced on Lean. R4-1 and R4-2 were reproduced with Lean probes. R4-3's harness ran every test class, TheLeanCheck included, so Lean ran for it. The report's `about` says only "which reproduced each"; the words "on Lean 4.29.1" in its about describe the lens. BOUNDARY-FIELD §9 repeats the overstatement.

findings.claim: "each followed by an adversarial verifier that reproduced every finding on Lean 4.29.1" (the third re-check)
findings.problem: One finding was confirmed with one of its sub-claims refuted.
findings.evidence: recheck3.json RC3-RULES-2 verdict: "Reproduced, except one sub-claim ... The refuted sub-claim: Python's private reading is covered, by TheTerms.test_auxiliaries_by_attachment, not by the cross test." All eight verdicts are real: true.
findings.fix: "... each followed by an adversarial verifier that confirmed all eight on Lean 4.29.1 (one sub-claim of RC3-RULES-2 refuted)".

verdict.reason: Confirmed, minor. All eight verdicts have real: true, but RC3-RULES-2's verdict begins "Reproduced, except one sub-claim" and refutes the sub-claim about Python's private reading, which TheTerms.test_auxiliaries_by_attachment covers. RC3-RULES-3 was "Confirmed by reading and by the stub run". So "reproduced every finding" leaves out a stated qualification. The report's own `about` and §9 use the same wording.

findings.claim: Evidence: "U4's 31 controls rerun on U4's build: output byte-identical"
findings.problem: The 31 are not all controls, and not all are U4's. They are the 31 cases of controls-run.log: rows 17 and 5, the controls, and 10 name-test queries. Of the controls, nine are U4's (adapted) and twelve are MV's.
findings.evidence: boundary/check/controls-run.log has 31 'ok' lines, ten of them 'admitted ...' name-test queries. BOUNDARY-FIELD §0: "Its 21 controls and 10 name-test queries come out as expected". §3.2: "They are U4's nine, adapted, and twelve more". §472: "U4's controls and the name-test queries come out as expected". The byte-identity itself holds: scratch mut4/controls.log and controls2.log equal the committed log.
findings.fix: "the controls on U4's build (controls-run.log's 31 cases: rows 17 and 5, the controls and 10 name-test queries) rerun after each re-check's fixes: output byte-identical". The same wording in BOUNDARY-FIELD §9's two paragraphs.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as to what the 31 are. boundary/check/controls-run.log has 31 'ok' lines: 21 cases (rows 17 and 5 and the controls) and 10 'admitted ...' name-test queries. BOUNDARY-FIELD §0 says "Its 21 controls and 10 name-test queries", and §3.2 says the controls are "U4's nine, adapted, and twelve more". U4's own log on u4-edge has nine controls and eight name queries, so the 31 are neither all controls nor all U4's. The byte-identity holds: scratch mut4/controls.log and controls2.log equal the committed controls-run.log, which is unchanged from main.

findings.claim: Evidence: "master_laws.py rerun on core receipts 20261031T013649.265381Z (RF-M.3's) and 20261031T054654.692180Z (HE2's) changes only the hashed inputs (boundary.py and boundary_check.lean)"
findings.problem: The branch's own rerun is on a third receipt, which the section does not name. The reruns on RF-M.3's and HE2's receipts happened only in clean-worktree rehearsals, and no output is kept.
findings.evidence: On mv-land, theories/becoming/results/data/master-laws.json has core_receipt 20261030T232750.486801Z (the branch's base 1aa84fd59; becoming-verification.json utc is the same). `git diff main...mv-land` changes only the boundary.py and boundary_check.lean hashes, and they match the current files' sha256. The HE2 rerun appears only in scratch ml9.log, whose counts equal main's master-laws.json.
findings.fix: "master_laws.py rerun on core 20261030T232750.486801Z (the branch's base) changes only the hashed inputs (boundary.py and boundary_check.lean); in the landing rehearsals, merged with main, reruns on RF-M.3's (20261031T013649.265381Z) and HE2's (20261031T054654.692180Z) receipts give the same figures". Or keep those outputs.

verdict.reason: Refuted in substance. The branch's own master-laws.json is at its base receipt 20261030T232750.486801Z. But the claim describes the landing merge, and the rehearsal shows it. In the clean rehearsal worktree mv-render (9053047be: mv-land at 863662705 merged with main at 9491cae33), master-laws.json is at HE2's receipt 20261031T054654.692180Z, and `git diff 9491cae33` shows only the boundary.py and boundary_check.lean hashes changed. Their values (9f70cc2b..., d1867fd5...) equal the current files' sha256. Scratch ml7.log (receipt 20261031T013649.265381Z) and ml9.log (HE2's, with counts equal to main's master-laws.json) are the RF-M.3 and HE2 reruns. The claim is true of what lands. Only where the reruns were done is unstated.

findings.claim: "sixteen mutations of the two copies, each caught" (Delta 4) and "sixteen mutations of the new parts, each caught" (Delta 5); "each as Lean 4.29.1 makes it on a probe"
findings.problem: No driver, probe or output for these is on the branch, so the section asserts results the branch cannot reproduce.

On the branch, the stub module's GENERATED realizes every new name on Lean 4.29.1 (half.induct ... evW.mutual_induct_unfolding, Nest._sizeOf_2_eq, below_1, brecOn_1 with go and eq, rec_1) except congr_eq_N, which no generated stub name has.

findings.claim: Evidence: "the verifiers' reproductions now pass (relC, relW, relO, relA, relE, relB) or fail (op.eq_1, Rp.brecOn.go, Cfg.elim) as §3.2 says"
findings.problem: What passes and fails are the stub module's adapted cases, not the verifiers' probes. §3.2 does not say these fail, nor that a macro's declaration passes; that comes from §3.0's attachment table and §8's list of controls.
findings.evidence: The cases are test_boundary.py's Edge stub, TheLeanCheck entries 18–23 (pass) and 24–27 (fail with op.eq_1, Rp.brecOn.go, op.eq_1, Cfg.elim). The verifiers' own probes were VA/VB/VC/VD in scratch (relC_at, relF_at ...). §9: "Their probe modules are carried, adapted, by the stub module". §3.2 mentions defaults and ack.eq_1 but not opaque, Prop brecOn or macro cases.
findings.fix: "the stub module's versions of the verifiers' cases pass (relC, relW, relO, relA, relE, relB) or fail (op.eq_1, Rp.brecOn.go, Cfg.elim) as §3.0 and §3.2 say (TheLeanCheck, entries 18 to 27)".

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The cases are the stub module's adapted versions: TheLeanCheck entries 18–23 (edge('relC'...'relB')) pass, and entries 24–27 fail with op.eq_1, Rp.brecOn.go, op.eq_1 and Cfg.elim (test_lifted_proofs_equation_lemmas_and_hygienic_names). The verifiers' own probes were VA–VD (relC_at, relW_at, relF_at ...) in scratch, and §9 says they are "carried, adapted, by the stub module". §3.2 test 9 states only the defaults and ack.eq_1 (relC, relW, relA). The constructor's optional argument, mutual definitions, the macro's name, the opaque's eq_1, the Prop brecOn's go and elim under a structure come from §3.0.

findings.claim: Boundary: "outside lists theorems whose immediate owner, or brecOn's owner, the dump lacks"
findings.problem: This is broader than the code. outside lists only theorems named as an auxiliary.
findings.evidence: boundary.outside: a theorem is listed only if its last component fullmatches an AUX pattern and printed(c[:-1]) is not in C (nor its private user name), or if it is go/eq under a brecOn(_N) whose owner printed(c[:-2]) is unknown. A theorem like Foo.bar under a missing Foo is not listed.
findings.fix: "outside lists theorems named as an auxiliary (a last component of AUX, or go/eq under a brecOn or brecOn_N) whose owner the dump lacks, read as printed and by a private name's user name".

verdict.reason: Confirmed by code and by a probe. boundary.outside lists a theorem only if its last component fullmatches an AUX pattern and printed(c[:-1]) is unknown (also by its private user name), or if it is go/eq under a brecOn(_N) whose owner printed(c[:-2]) is unknown. Run on {Becoming.Space.bar (thm), Becoming.Space.inj (thm), Becoming.Space.brecOn.eq (thm), Becoming.Space.brecOn (def)}, it returned {Becoming.Space.inj, Becoming.Space.brecOn.eq}. Space.bar under the missing Space is not listed.

findings.fix: "... (Nat.fold.eq_def), and an _arg_pusher under Init's PSigma.casesOn or PSum.casesOn in a package module's private names".

findings.problem: The branch also changes §3.6, which Delta (5) itself cites (R4-4), as well as §3.2's "On U4's forms" paragraph and the status line.

findings.fix: "The design is BOUNDARY-FIELD §3.0, §3.2 (test 9 and U4's forms), §3.6, §8 and §9."

verdict.reason: Confirmed (missing). git diff main...mv-land on BOUNDARY-FIELD.md also rewrites: §3.6 'The input' and 'When it cannot run', which Delta (5) itself cites for R4-4; §3.2's 'On U4's forms' paragraph ("rerun four times"); and the status line ("re-checked four times"). Commit f3de580e6's message lists "§3.0, §3.2 test 9, §3.6, §8 and §9".

findings.claim: Delta (5) tests: "...; sixteen mutations of the new parts, each caught; 61 tests."
findings.problem: The fourth's fixes added no test method. The four new tests, 57 to 61, came with the third's fixes, yet (4) gives no count and (5) reads as if the fourth brought the count to 61.
findings.evidence: Test methods: 57 at §472 (and 1aa84fd59), 61 at 26977f25a (new: test_the_names_the_dump_cannot_settle, test_an_auxiliary_of_a_declaration_the_dump_lacks, test_the_lean_checks_kinds_for_d2, test_lifted_proofs_equation_lemmas_and_hygienic_names), 61 at f3de580e6 and the tip. `python3 -B -m unittest tools.research.tests.test_boundary` ran 61, OK (skipped=1).
findings.fix: In (4): "...; 61 tests (57 at §472)". In (5): "the cases added to existing tests (61 still)".

verdict.reason: Confirmed. test_boundary.py has 57 test methods on main and at 1aa84fd59, and 61 at 26977f25a. The four new ones (test_the_names_the_dump_cannot_settle, test_an_auxiliary_of_a_declaration_the_dump_lacks, test_the_lean_checks_kinds_for_d2, test_lifted_proofs_equation_lemmas_and_hygienic_names) came with the third re-check's fixes. f3de580e6 and HEAD still have 61. `python3 -B -m unittest tools.research.tests.test_boundary` ran 61 tests, OK (skipped=1). The figure is true of the branch, but placed under (5) it reads as if the fourth's fixes reached it.

findings.claim: Evidence: "research check --strict-fresh, links and the suite (304 tests) pass in a clean worktree"
findings.problem: The branch holds no record of these checks. The last complete rehearsal failed the link check, and the rehearsal on the tip had not finished.
findings.evidence: Discovery counts 304 tests (`unittest discover -s tools/research/tests -p 'test_*.py'`). Scratch rehearse9.status: "cmp 0, strict 0, links 2, test 0". l9.log shows 6 broken links in the kit's .md drafts. Links passed after 863662705 (l10.log), but 416b0af81 came later. rehearse11 (cs11.log) was still running at the time of this check.
findings.fix: Keep the sentence only once the rehearsal on the tip (or the landing merge) passes all three. Otherwise say "pass in a clean worktree at 863662705 (links) and before it (check, suite)".

verdict.reason: Refuted at the time of this check. The finding's basis is out of date. Rehearsal 11, in the clean worktree mv-render (9053047be: mv-land at 863662705 merged with main), finished with status "render 0, strict 0, links 0, test 0". l11/cs11 passed and t11.log says "Ran 304 tests ... OK (skipped=2)". Discovery on the branch also counts 304. The only later commit, 416b0af81, changes just the .txt draft and the JSON report in the MV folder, which neither the link check (Markdown only) nor the suite reads. Main has since moved (39bd9ac9c, d3a502880), so the landing merge still needs its usual rerun. That is procedure, not an error in the sentence.

findings.claim: The design the section cites (BOUNDARY-FIELD §8, §9 R4-3 row): "each new pattern under a kind it must not attach to, among the names not generated"; §8 "the code gets an independent review and three re-checks"
findings.problem: Both points are overstated or stale in the file the section points readers to. Several new patterns have no wrong-kind negative, the Lean copy's congr_eq_N has no positive, and §8 still counts three re-checks.
findings.evidence: NOT_GENERATED (66) has wrong-kind cases for induct, fun_cases, eq_unfold, _sizeOf_N_eq, brecOn_N, below_N and rec_N. It has none for mutual_induct, mutual_induct_unfolding, induct_unfolding, fun_cases_unfolding or congr_eq_N; congr_eq_N has only the near miss half.congr_eq_. No congr_eq_N is among the 69 generated, so only Python's TheTerms tests it. The status line says "re-checked four times" and §9 has four re-check tables.
findings.fix: Narrow the R4-3 row to the patterns that have negatives, or add negatives for the others and a congr_eq_N case to the stub. In §8: "an independent review and four re-checks; the third's and fourth's findings land after the field, as MV's follow-up".

verdict.reason: Confirmed. §8 line 497 still says "three re-checks ... The third re-check's findings land after the field", while the status line says "re-checked four times" and §9 has four re-check tables. Among the 66 NOT_GENERATED names, the new patterns with wrong-kind negatives are induct (Tone.induct, seven.induct), fun_cases (comm.fun_cases), eq_unfold (op.eq_unfold), _sizeOf_N_eq, below_N, brecOn_N and rec_N (half.*, Onward.mk.rec_1). congr_eq_N has none, only the near miss half.congr_eq_. No congr_eq_N is among the 69 GENERATED either, so the Lean copy's congr_eq_ branch has no positive (only Python's TheTerms has X.match_1.congr_eq_1). By R4-3's own standard (negatives apart from the group), induct_unfolding, mutual_induct, mutual_induct_unfolding and fun_cases_unfolding also lack their own negatives in the Lean list, though Python reads them through the induct and fun_cases alternations.

findings.claim: Evidence: "research check --strict-fresh, links and the suite (304 tests) pass in a clean worktree"

Until then: "links and the suite pass; --strict-fresh fails on _process/research/README.md (327 for 328 files; tighten.json was added after the render)".

The cause: 03b19583f added ra-first-screen/tighten.json and also touched the index, so the index was rendered before tighten.json was added. `research.py links` passes with an empty broken list. findings.claim: The screen's "No outside review yet", and the evidence line choosing it over "internal", "which would suggest a human review the account says has not happened"
findings.problem: The repository's own live record names an outside review. As worded, the screen says something a live record contradicts. What the account says has not happened is a human review.
findings.evidence: theories/becoming/results/records/least-loss-rest.md:71 and .json: "The outside review of 19 October 2026 (R20) and an outside reader named the rest laws' dependence on whole-number amounts". BECOMING-SIGNIFICANCE-REVIEW.md:6: "On 19 October an outside reviewer (a friend's GPT model) concluded...". 08 §11 (08-METHOD.md:589): "Every review so far is by AI ... No human review is claimed". Overview :239: "No review so far has been by a human reader". tighten.json's precision draft warned: "If any past review came from a party outside the work, it would need checking against the review ledger". That check is not recorded.
findings.fix: Have the screen say "No human review yet." (it names no person and no AI, and matches 08 §11 and the overview), and say so in (9) and the evidence line. Otherwise, the section should state the R20 outside review and why "outside" still holds.
